source.title: Dynamical Isometry is Achieved in Residual Networks in a Universal Way for any Activation Function
source.authors: W. Tarnowski; P. Warchol; Stanislaw Jastrzebski; J. Tabor; M. Nowak

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper and appendices; some equations and figure content are flattened, but the relevant training-curve descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether activation-dependent initialization affects training dynamics in residual networks, extending initialization results to a residual-network setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training-accuracy curves and states that sigmoid optimization is significantly slower. It does not report training classification error or test the other listed versions. Jacobian-spectrum results concern initialization measurements, not training error.
record.test_reason: The study measures initialization spectra and training dynamics in fully connected residual networks. V4 specifies plain networks and faster learning or greater trainable depth; these experiments instead test whether matching initial Jacobian spectra makes activation-dependent learning curves more similar. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the training experiments. The paper's main conclusion is that a universal initialization spectrum is achievable across activation functions in its residual-network model. Matching that spectrum makes learning curves for similar activations more alike, while sigmoid remains slower and the initial spectrum does not fully determine training performance.
record.recipe_differences: Residual fully connected CIFAR-10 networks with activation-dependent initialization; tests training accuracy across activation functions rather than plain-network learning speed or trainable depth.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation function and initialization choice affect the training-accuracy curves; sigmoid is slower, and equalizing effective cumulant makes curves more similar than using equal weight variances.

fits_no_version.finding: With effective cumulant fixed at 0.125, sigmoid residual networks optimize substantially more slowly than networks using most other activations; the authors attribute this to activation growth and saturation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matching initial Jacobian spectra across activation functions does not guarantee equal optimization speed in fully connected residual networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation-specific initialization producing a common effective cumulant makes learning curves for similar activations more alike than initialization with equal weight variances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial Jacobian spectra confound comparisons of activation-dependent learning dynamics in fully connected residual networks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: Training-accuracy results are shown as plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments use a simplified fully connected residual architecture; the authors leave more general ResNet architectures for future work. No training-error result is reported.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including corrupted or random labels, and dependence on size, early stopping or regularization. Training accuracy is reported and implies training error, but the models are fully connected residual networks.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction with extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation in plain convolutional networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.

Faster learning and greater trainable depth from activation-matched initialization in plain networks; orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian training comparisons; training 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
Loss recovery, curvature changes and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, including edge-of-stability training.

Training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with versus without batch normalization, including the Fixup comparison. Section V analyzes initialization spectra rather than these training outcomes.

record.verdict_notes: Neither residual-network training curves nor initialization-only Jacobian measurements justify a verdict on V4 as written. The record's statement that no training-error result is reported is misleading: classification error is one minus training accuracy, although these experiments still fall outside V1's specified architecture.

versions.untested_parts: No reported training classification error, CIFAR-100, corrupted labels, random labels, or comparison involving smaller models or early stopping.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or comparison of student and teacher widths.

No plain-network comparison, depth-related training-error comparison, or shortcut ablation. The batch-normalization discussion is theoretical and does not test the stated residual-network training claim.
Tests residual networks on CIFAR-10, not plain networks or trainable depth. Does not compare Gaussian and orthogonal weights of equal variance or test 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
No learning-rate stability-limit, curvature, sharpness, or divergence experiment.
No empirical batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparison or higher-learning-rate tolerance test.

rows.subject: Residual fully connected network with Sigmoid activation
rows.size_stated: 10 and 20 residual blocks; width not stated for these experiments
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with activation-specific initialization set to effective cumulant c = 0.125; training accuracy compared across activations.

conditions.value: starting rate either 10−3 or 10−4; dropped by factor of 10 after epochs 80, 120, and 160

rows.baseline: Networks with other activation functions at c = 0.125; exact values not stated.
rows.value: Sigmoid activation led to significantly slower optimization; figure shows training accuracy, figure-only values.
rows.note: Authors state that most activation functions have similar training-accuracy evolution, with sigmoid significantly slower. Curves are not numerically tabulated.
rows.check: Slower sigmoid optimization relative to other activations in residual networks does not measure V4's benefit of matched initialization in plain networks. The reported slowdown is valid, but its classification as a partial V4 effect is unsupported.

rows.subject: Residual fully connected networks with various activation functions
rows.size_stated: 10 and 20 residual blocks; width not stated for these experiments
rows.operation_detail: Compared learning curves for activation-specific initialization at c = 0.125 with a setup using the same weight standard deviation across activations.

conditions.value: activation-specific c = 0.125 versus constant standard deviation σ = 1/√(LN)

rows.baseline: Constant weight standard deviation σ = 1/√(LN); figure-only values.
rows.value: With c = 0.125, similar-characteristic activations had markedly coinciding learning behavior; with constant standard deviations, activation-dependent learning dynamics differed, especially at the beginning. Figure-only values.
rows.locator: Section IV.B; Figure 4 (top and middle panels); Appendix E, Figure 7
rows.note: Comparison is described in text, but curve values are not reported numerically. The paper says the same effective cumulant makes learning dynamics more similar, not that all activation functions train equally fast.
rows.check: Matching effective cumulants makes learning curves across activations more similar; this does not establish faster learning or increased trainable depth. The architecture is fully connected and residual, outside V4's specified plain-network setting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Residual fully connected CIFAR-10 networks with activation-specific c = 0.125 initialization
reader_labels.reason: Most activation functions had similar training-accuracy evolution, but sigmoid optimization was significantly slower (R1); matched initialization made dynamics more similar across activations than constant weight variance did (R2). This is a residual-network extension, not evidence about plain-network trainable depth.
